en.greeting: Hi! Today we learn words for work, study and technology, so you can talk about your day at the office or on campus.

steps.title: At work
steps.text: Let's start with the people, tasks and places of a work day.
steps.body: At work you **have a meeting** with your **manager** (boss) and your **colleagues**, you **write a report**, and you finish before the **deadline** (the last time to finish a task). You work **in an office** or **in a factory**, maybe on **the night shift**, or you **work from home**. Careful: *pabrik* is **factory**, not *fabric* (fabric = kain).

steps.title: A work day
steps.text: Read these sentences out loud.
steps.body: To say your job, use **work as a/an** + job. Indonesian *bekerja sebagai* has no *seorang*, but English still needs **a/an**: **an** before a vowel sound (*an engineer*), **a** before a consonant sound (*a programmer*).

examples.en: I have a meeting with my manager at ten.
examples.id: Saya ada rapat dengan atasan saya jam sepuluh.

examples.en: Budi is writing a report. The deadline is Friday.
examples.id: Budi sedang membuat laporan. Tenggat waktunya hari Jumat.

examples.en: My sister works as an engineer in a factory.
examples.id: Kakak saya bekerja sebagai insinyur di pabrik.

examples.en: Dimas works as a programmer. He works from home on Fridays.
examples.id: Dimas bekerja sebagai programmer. Dia kerja dari rumah setiap hari Jumat.

examples.en: This week Pak Joko is on the morning shift.
examples.id: Minggu ini Pak Joko masuk sif pagi.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Choose the correct sentence.

question.prompt: Sari answers the phone and welcomes guests at a hotel in Bali. Which sentence is correct?
question.explanation: One job needs **a/an**, also after **as**. *Receptionist* starts with an 'r' sound, a consonant, so it's **a receptionist**. **an** is only for a vowel sound.

steps.title: School and university
steps.text: Now the words for school and campus.
steps.body: At school you have a **teacher**; at university you have a **lecturer** (dosen; Americans say *professor*). A **test** is short (ulangan); an **exam** is big (UAS, UTBK). **Skripsi** is a **thesis**, not a *script* (naskah film). **Homework** has no -s: say **a lot of homework** (*a lot of* = banyak), and you **do** homework, you don't *make* it.

steps.title: On campus
steps.text: Here are the words in real sentences.
steps.body: *maths* and *favourite* are British; Americans write *math* and *favorite*.

examples.en: My favourite subject is biology.
examples.id: Mata pelajaran favorit saya biologi.

examples.en: We have a maths test every Friday.
examples.id: Kami ada ulangan matematika setiap hari Jumat.

examples.en: Rina is in her sixth semester. She's writing her thesis.
examples.id: Rina semester enam. Dia sedang menulis skripsi.

examples.en: Our teacher gives us a lot of homework.
examples.id: Guru kami memberi kami banyak PR.

examples.en: Budi does his homework at the library.
examples.id: Budi mengerjakan PR-nya di perpustakaan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Who is Bu Ani?

question.prompt: Dimas studies at Universitas Indonesia. Bu Ani teaches him economics there. Bu Ani is Dimas's ___.
question.explanation: A person who teaches at a university is a **lecturer** (dosen). A **classmate** studies with you, and a **student** learns; Bu Ani teaches.

steps.title: Build the question
steps.text: Ask a friend about homework.

question.solution: How much homework do you have?
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Berapa banyak PR-mu?
question.explanation: Homework is uncountable (we don't count it one by one), so we ask **How much**, not *How many*, and **homework** has no -s.

steps.title: Technology words
steps.text: Last group: the technology you use every day.
steps.body: Many words are the same as in Indonesian: **email**, **app**, **password**, **click**. **Download** = from the internet to your phone; **upload** = from your phone to the internet. You **attach a file** to an email. Important: the action is **log in**, two words (*I log in, she logs in*). **login**, one word, is only a thing: *the login page*.

steps.title: On my phone
steps.text: Read them and notice log in and login.
steps.body: *an email, an app* (vowel sound), but *a password, a file*.

examples.en: I can't log in because I can't remember my password.
examples.id: Saya tidak bisa masuk karena saya lupa kata sandi saya.

examples.en: Open the login page and type your password.
examples.id: Buka halaman login dan ketik kata sandimu.

examples.en: Please attach your CV to the email.
examples.id: Tolong lampirkan CV-mu ke email.

examples.en: Rina uploads photos to Instagram every day.
examples.id: Rina mengunggah foto ke Instagram setiap hari.

examples.en: Download the app and click Start.
examples.id: Unduh aplikasinya dan klik Start.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pick the right form.

question.prompt: Budi types his password and ___ to the app.
question.explanation: It's an action, so the verb is two words: **log in**. Budi = he, so add **-s** to *log*: **logs in**. *login* (one word) is only a thing, like *the login page*.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here are all the words on one page. Save it!

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? Try these exercises and videos about jobs, university and the internet.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita belajar kata-kata tentang kerja, kuliah dan teknologi, supaya kamu bisa menceritakan harimu di kantor atau di kampus.

steps.title: Di tempat kerja
steps.text: Kita mulai dari orang, tugas dan tempat dalam satu hari kerja.
steps.body: Di tempat kerja kamu **have a meeting** (ada rapat) dengan **manager** (atasan) dan **colleagues** (rekan kerja), kamu **write a report** (membuat laporan), dan selesai sebelum **deadline** (tenggat waktu). Kamu kerja **in an office** (di kantor) atau **in a factory** (di pabrik), mungkin **the night shift** (sif malam), atau **work from home**. Hati-hati: *pabrik* itu **factory**, bukan *fabric* (fabric = kain).

steps.title: Satu hari kerja
steps.text: Bacalah kalimat-kalimat ini dengan suara keras.
steps.body: Untuk menyebut pekerjaan, pakai **work as a/an** + pekerjaan. *Bekerja sebagai* tidak pakai *seorang*, tapi bahasa Inggris tetap butuh **a/an**: **an** sebelum bunyi vokal (*an engineer*), **a** sebelum bunyi konsonan (*a programmer*).

examples.en: I have a meeting with my manager at ten.
examples.id: Saya ada rapat dengan atasan saya jam sepuluh.

examples.en: Budi is writing a report. The deadline is Friday.
examples.id: Budi sedang membuat laporan. Tenggat waktunya hari Jumat.

examples.en: My sister works as an engineer in a factory.
examples.id: Kakak saya bekerja sebagai insinyur di pabrik.

examples.en: Dimas works as a programmer. He works from home on Fridays.
examples.id: Dimas bekerja sebagai programmer. Dia kerja dari rumah setiap hari Jumat.

examples.en: This week Pak Joko is on the morning shift.
examples.id: Minggu ini Pak Joko masuk sif pagi.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pilih kalimat yang benar.

question.prompt: Sari mengangkat telepon dan menyambut tamu di sebuah hotel di Bali. Kalimat mana yang benar?
question.explanation: Satu pekerjaan butuh **a/an**, juga setelah **as**. *Receptionist* diawali bunyi 'r', yaitu konsonan, jadi **a receptionist**. **an** hanya untuk bunyi vokal.

steps.title: Sekolah dan kuliah
steps.text: Sekarang kata-kata untuk sekolah dan kampus.
steps.body: Di sekolah ada **teacher** (guru); di kampus ada **lecturer** (dosen; orang Amerika bilang *professor*). **Test** itu pendek (ulangan); **exam** itu besar (UAS, UTBK). **Skripsi** adalah **thesis**, bukan *script* (naskah film). **Homework** tanpa -s: bilang **a lot of homework** (*a lot of* = banyak), dan PR itu di-**do** (dikerjakan), bukan *make*.

steps.title: Di kampus
steps.text: Ini kata-katanya dalam kalimat nyata.
steps.body: *maths* dan *favourite* itu ejaan British; orang Amerika menulis *math* dan *favorite*.

examples.id: Mata pelajaran favorit saya biologi.

examples.en: We have a maths test every Friday.
examples.id: Kami ada ulangan matematika setiap hari Jumat.

examples.en: Rina is in her sixth semester. She's writing her thesis.
examples.id: Rina semester enam. Dia sedang menulis skripsi.

examples.en: Our teacher gives us a lot of homework.
examples.id: Guru kami memberi kami banyak PR.

examples.en: Budi does his homework at the library.
examples.id: Budi mengerjakan PR-nya di perpustakaan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Siapa Bu Ani?

question.prompt: Dimas kuliah di Universitas Indonesia. Bu Ani mengajar dia ekonomi di sana. Lengkapi: Bu Ani is Dimas's ___.
question.explanation: Orang yang mengajar di universitas adalah **lecturer** (dosen). **Classmate** adalah teman sekelas, dan **student** adalah orang yang belajar; Bu Ani mengajar.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaannya
steps.text: Tanyakan temanmu tentang PR.

question.solution: How much homework do you have?
question.explanation: Homework tidak bisa dihitung satu per satu (uncountable), jadi kita bertanya **How much**, bukan *How many*, dan **homework** tanpa -s.

steps.title: Kata-kata teknologi
steps.text: Kelompok terakhir: teknologi yang kamu pakai setiap hari.
steps.body: Banyak kata sama dengan bahasa Indonesia: **email**, **app**, **password**, **click**. **Download** = dari internet ke HP-mu; **upload** = dari HP-mu ke internet. Kamu **attach a file** (melampirkan file) ke email. Penting: tindakannya **log in**, dua kata (*I log in, she logs in*). **login**, satu kata, hanya untuk benda: *the login page*.

steps.title: Di HP-ku
steps.text: Baca, lalu perhatikan log in dan login.
steps.body: *an email, an app* (bunyi vokal), tapi *a password, a file*.

steps.text: Pilih bentuk yang benar.

question.explanation: Ini tindakan, jadi kata kerjanya dua kata: **log in**. Budi = he, jadi *log* ditambah **-s**: **logs in**. *login* (satu kata) hanya untuk benda, seperti *the login page*.
